brief.headline: Elmer's blood pressure has risen across three readings (175/88 on 2026-11-07) with missed evening doses, and he is withdrawing and feeling down after a friend's death, while his caregiver Rosa reports exhaustion and asks for respite.

items.statement: Three elevated BP readings in the period, rising: 158/88 (2026-09-26), 167/97 (2026-10-25), 175/88 (2026-11-07), against a 140/90 threshold. On 2026-11-07 the RN noted Elmer admits missing evening doses some days and flagged the antihypertensive regimen for PCP review.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record has the three BP readings and dates and the 140/90 threshold. The 2026-11-07 RN note supports the missed evening doses and the flag for PCP review.

items.statement: On 2026-11-19 Elmer told the social worker he feels "down" and does not want to leave the house since a close friend died last month. The social worker plans a depression screen and grief support. On 2026-11-17 the day center reported he missed 4 of the last 8 scheduled days and, when present, is quiet and leaves activities early.
items.verifier_note: The 11-19 social work note and the 11-17 attendance note support every detail: feeling down, the friend's death last month, the plan to screen and offer grief support, 4 of 8 days missed, and quiet behavior with early departures.

items.statement: On 2026-10-04 Rosa (spouse and primary caregiver) reported exhaustion, poor sleep and worry about managing evenings alone, and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed. The evidence shows no outcome yet.
items.verifier_note: The 10-04 note supports Rosa's exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings, the respite request, and the discussion of respite options and a support group. The note records no outcome.

items.statement: No medications were started or stopped from 2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30. The BP rise and missed evening doses have not yet led to a documented regimen change.
items.verifier_note: The medications record shows nothing started or stopped since 09-01. The RN note shows a flag for PCP review but no documented regimen change.

questions_for_team: What is the PCP's plan for the antihypertensive regimen, and how can the team address the missed evening doses (for example the dosing schedule or reminders)?
When will the depression screen be done, and who will follow up on grief support?
Could the mood change and the missed evening doses be related, and does the team need to look at both together?
What respite arrangement can be offered to Rosa, especially for evenings, and has she taken up the support group?
Should day center outreach or transport support be added to help Elmer attend?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all events since the last IDT review: falls, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions, with dates and reasons.
Falls and fall-risk screen: any falls or near-falls in the window, injuries, and whether fall-risk assessment was repeated. Relevant given age 82, osteoporosis, and cardiac medications.

Chest pain and cardiac events: any use of nitroglycerin spray in the window (frequency and dates), new chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, or cardiology visits, given ischemic heart disease with clopidogrel, metoprolol, and simvastatin.
Bleeding and antiplatelet review: any bleeding, bruising, melena, hematuria, or nosebleeds on clopidogrel; flag for team discussion if reported.
Blood pressure trend: all recorded BP readings in the window versus prior baseline, with attention to low readings or orthostatic symptoms on metoprolol, and to hypertension control.
Heart rate trend and any bradycardia or dizziness noted on metoprolol succinate 100 mg.

Kidney function: most recent eGFR and creatinine, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and dates of labs, given CKD stage 2 with microalbuminuria and diabetic kidney disease. Check whether labs are due in this period.

Diabetes-related monitoring: HbA1c and glucose values, since diabetic kidney disease is listed but no diabetes medication appears on the active list. Confirm whether this reflects a reconciliation gap or a deliberate plan, and flag for clinician review.

Medication reconciliation: compare the active list (metoprolol, clopidogrel, doxycycline, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin) with any starts, stops, or dose changes in the window. Note doxycycline has a 1948 start date and confirm whether it is still active and why. Check for any new NSAIDs or nephrotoxic agents given CKD.
Lipid and statin review: most recent lipid panel and whether simvastatin 20 mg is still the intended dose given ischemic heart disease; flag for clinician discussion without recommending a change.
Weight and BMI trend: measured weights in the window versus baseline, given obesity (BMI 30+) and cardiometabolic conditions.

Osteoporosis care: check whether bone density results, calcium and vitamin D status, and any fracture history or antiresorptive therapy are documented and up to date; none of these appear on the active medication list.
Sinusitis: any recent episodes, antibiotic courses, or ENT visits in the window, given chronic sinusitis and penicillin allergy.
Function and ADLs: any change in ADL or IADL status (bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, medication management, meal preparation, driving), and whether a functional reassessment is due.
Cognition and mood: any cognitive screen results, new confusion, or mood screen (e.g., PHQ-2/PHQ-9) in the window, and whether screening is due.

Social and caregiver situation: living situation changes, caregiver availability or strain, transportation barriers, and any home safety concerns. Confirm contact information and emergency contact are current.
Attendance and engagement: PACE day-center attendance rate in the window, missed appointments, and transportation issues.
Allergy record: confirm penicillin V reaction (wheal) and egg allergy are current; note the 'allergic disposition' finding for reconciliation.
Care-plan items due: list all care-plan goals, IDT review items, assessments, and vaccinations due or overdue in or before the review date of 2026-11-30, and flag any that are past due.
Summarize for the IDT: list what changed in the window, each item needing team discussion, and each data gap, framed as questions for clinicians rather than recommendations.
